column5: Kenya TJRC (2013) says the Mau Mau 'caused the death of at least 14,000 Africans, 29 Asians and 95 Europeans' while calling the figures debatable; the course uses Reader/Anderson counts of about 2,000 loyalist Kikuyu and 32 white civilians. The TJRC text is a compilation of secondary writers without a method, and its 14,000 may include Kikuyu killed in the wider war. Keep the course figures, flag the TJRC range as a contested compilation [CONTESTED]

TJRC: Corfield Tribunal recorded 11,503 Mau Mau dead (probably an undercount); about 1,000 hanged; 150,000 to 320,000 detained in more than 50 camps; Lari, 26/03/1953, about 400 killed, mostly women and children; Hola 1959, 11 detainees clubbed to death and 77 permanently injured. It follows Elkins, Anderson and Hornsby. It dates the war 1952-55 in one place and ends it with Kimathi in 10/1956, so its own dates differ

TJRC: the British removed and hid most records of the war on the eve of independence; Kenyatta's government did not honour Mau Mau, amnesty for fighters ran to 01/1964 (over 2,000 surrendered), and the 2011 British court ruling let Kenyan claimants sue. The Commission traces Mau Mau to land alienation: Crown Lands Ordinance 1915, about 5 million acres taken by 1914, about 294,000 Kikuyu outside the reserves in 1948 (29 per cent)

TJRC on independent Kenya: independence 12/12/1963, republic with Kenyatta as President a year later (confirms the course's check on Reader); Pio Gama Pinto killed 24/02/1965, Tom Mboya 05/07/1969, Kisumu shootings 25/10/1969, J M Kariuki 1975; one-party state de jure from 1982 and ended 1991; 1982 coup attempt cost an estimated 600 to 1,800 lives
